newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee closes up at 35.89/90 against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee closes up at 35.89/90 against dollar.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed at 35.89/90 per dollar on Friday, up from the opening level of 35.92/94, dealers said.
The day opened at Thursday's closing level and most banks, which were hit by late evening bids by a Calcutta bank on Thursday, were busy covering their short positions.
"Many banks also expected them (the Calcutta bank) to hit again today," said a dealer. Some dealers were anticipating the dollar to test the 36 per dollar level.
But the Calcutta bank abstained, and the rupee recovered as banks unwound their positions as the day progressed.
The rupee saw a low of 35.94 in early morning deals. One dealer reported stray deals at 35.8850 level, the day's high.
The forward dollar market ended the day at the opening level despite some intra-day fluctuations, dealers said. The six-month annualised premium closed steady at 6.75 percent.
"After a steady 35.66/70 closing during July to October, the rupee has closed weaker at 35.88 in December," a foreign bank said in its forex commentary on Friday.
"Corporates would look to hedge their exposure keeping the interest rate differential in mind," it said.
It said the fall in six-month premia reflected a 50 basis point cut in banks' cash reserve requirement effective Saturday.
"We expect paying (of premia for forward dollar) to emerge on dips," the bank said.
